adams-county-board-roster.summary: Adams County's board card names one of your three district members — the seat filled at the last election that covered it. The other two aren't named.
adams-county-board-roster.why: The county's site turns away automated visits, so its own member list can't be read. The names shown come from certified election results, which cover only the seats voted on in 2024; the 2022 results that filled the rest aren't published.
adams-county-board-roster.wanted: The fourteen members elected in November 2022, by district — from the county's own certified canvass for that election, or from any member list a program is allowed to read.

aurora-council-contact.area: Aurora (Kane, DuPage, Kendall and Will counties)
aurora-council-contact.summary: Aurora's 12 council members show with the right ward, but with no phone number or e-mail address.
aurora-council-contact.why: The city's site opens normally in a browser but refuses automated visits, and the ward map data carries no contact details.
aurora-council-contact.wanted: Phone and e-mail for the 12 aldermen — a council directory from any of the four county clerks Aurora spans would do it.

blocked-crawlers.summary: Board member lists for McHenry, Kendall and DeKalb are checked by hand rather than weekly, so a change can take longer to appear. The names on the cards are current.
blocked-crawlers.why: All three county directories turn away the automated check that refreshes every other roster each week.
blocked-crawlers.wanted: A member list any of the three counties lets a program read — a data file, or a mirror of the same directory.

bond-county-board-districts.summary: Bond County's five board districts aren't drawn, so the card can't tell you which one you're in. All five members are named on the county's own site.
bond-county-board-districts.why: The county publishes no district map, and its election results show four precincts split between two districts, so no published boundary would draw the lines.
bond-county-board-districts.wanted: The county's 2021 board redistricting map or ordinance — or any description of how those four split precincts divide.

boone-fire-belvidere-city.summary: Inside Belvidere the fire card now says the city runs its own fire department rather than naming a county district it does not belong to. The county's own map still shows the city as district 2.
boone-fire-belvidere-city.why: The county's fire map covers every acre with five districts, city included, where the county's own tax roll shows no fire district at all. The card no longer repeats that; the county's data still says it.
boone-fire-belvidere-city.wanted: Confirmation from Boone County that Belvidere is a hole in its fire map — the card is corrected either way, but the county's own layer still draws the city as district 2, and only the county can fix that at the source.

boone-fire-names.summary: Boone County's five fire protection districts show by number instead of by name.
boone-fire-names.why: The map data carries no names, and the county's tax reports name six districts to the map's five, so a name matched by position could land on the wrong one.
boone-fire-names.wanted: A county statement tying each mapped district to its name, including where Cherry Valley Fire's Boone territory sits.

brown-precinct-geometry.summary: Brown County's 14 voting precincts aren't drawn on the map.
brown-precinct-geometry.why: The county publishes no precinct map, and the census boundaries that would stand in for one can't tell which of two recently renamed precincts is which.
brown-precinct-geometry.wanted: One answer from the County Clerk: when Missouri and Ripley precincts became Missouri-Ripley 1 and 2, was that a rename, or were the lines redrawn?

bureau-county-board-districts.summary: Bureau County's 18 board districts aren't drawn, so the card can't say which one you're in. The county does name its members and their parties.
bureau-county-board-districts.why: The county's public map has no district lines drawn on it, and the digital file is sold under terms that forbid republishing anything built from it.
bureau-county-board-districts.wanted: Permission to use the county's board district file on a free public map — or a plain list of which precincts and blocks make up each district.

captcha-county-commissioner-contact.summary: Union's five commissioners and Williamson's three are named on the County card, with no phone number or e-mail address for any of them.
captcha-county-commissioner-contact.why: Both counties' websites turn away automated visits behind a challenge page. The names come from the counties' own certified election results, which publish no contact details.
captcha-county-commissioner-contact.wanted: A phone number or e-mail for each commissioner — from either county's own site read by a person, or from a clerk's directory a program is allowed to read.

carroll-special-districts.summary: Carroll County's fire and park districts aren't shown. Its seven library districts are.
carroll-special-districts.why: The county sells its map data rather than publishing it, so nothing free carries its fire or park boundaries.
carroll-special-districts.wanted: Fire and park district boundaries the county will let a free civic site use.

carroll-ward-geometry.summary: Savanna, Mount Carroll and Lanark all elect aldermen by ward, and none of the three sets of ward lines can be drawn here.
carroll-ward-geometry.why: Savanna publishes its wards as a 1977 written description and a scanned map and keeps the digital copy private; the other two publish nothing usable.
carroll-ward-geometry.wanted: Current ward boundaries for any of the three — for Savanna, the map file it already holds, or word that the 1977 description still stands.

champaign-piatt-ccgisc-license.concept: County board districts and voting precincts
champaign-piatt-ccgisc-license.summary: Champaign's and Piatt's board districts and precincts are complete, current and online — and we aren't allowed to republish them.
champaign-piatt-ccgisc-license.why: Both counties' maps are run by a GIS consortium that sells the data under a licence forbidding public redisplay, and each county says the consortium holds the files.
champaign-piatt-ccgisc-license.wanted: Written permission from the consortium, or the same boundaries released by either county under public records law.

chicago-amenity-phones.summary: Fire station cards don't show a phone number.
chicago-amenity-phones.why: The national dataset these station locations come from has no phone number in it — it's missing at the source, not undisplayed.
chicago-amenity-phones.wanted: A Chicago Fire Department or region-wide station list that includes public phone numbers.

christian-county-board-districts.summary: Christian County's board districts aren't drawn, so the card can't tell you which one you're in, and the county names only its chairman and vice-chairman.
christian-county-board-districts.why: The county's current district map is a picture with no readable lines on it, and the one readable file beside it is the previous decade's plan.
christian-county-board-districts.wanted: The 2021 districts as map data — or one answer from the Clerk: which precinct was Taylorville 9 carved out of? Either one draws the map.

clark-board-contact.summary: Clark County board cards name your member and the election that seated them, and give the county switchboard rather than a direct phone or e-mail.
clark-board-contact.why: The county's only board list is a scanned image, so each member's contact details can be read by eye and not by machine — and one e-mail address isn't legible at all.
clark-board-contact.wanted: The seven members' county phone numbers and e-mail addresses in any typed form, plus the name of the board chairman.

clark-precinct-polling.summary: Clark County precinct cards name your precinct and its board district, but not where you vote.
clark-precinct-polling.why: The county's only polling place list is from 2018, and sending a voter to an eight-year-old address is worse than saying nothing.
clark-precinct-polling.wanted: Clark County's current polling places paired with its 23 precinct names, in any typed form.

clinton-precinct-geometry.summary: Clinton County's board districts are drawn; its voting precincts aren't.
clinton-precinct-geometry.why: Five Brookside precincts were merged into three, and no published source says which of the old ones became which, so a precinct card couldn't name yours.
clinton-precinct-geometry.wanted: Which of the old Brookside precincts make up each of the three today — a sentence from the Clerk, or any precinct boundary file.

county-board-office-addresses.summary: Most county board cards give you no address to visit — 50 county board cards name no office at all.
county-board-office-addresses.why: Thirteen counties publish an address for their board; the rest publish none. Where a county prints members' HOME addresses instead — and several do — those are never shown here.
county-board-office-addresses.wanted: A board office address per county, or the building where members hold office hours — one shared address per county is usually the honest answer.

crete-municipal-clerk.summary: Crete's card names the Village President, six Trustees and the Treasurer — but not the Village Clerk, and gives no village hall address or phone.
crete-municipal-clerk.why: The county directory's Crete entry loses its top section when read by machine, and the village's own site turns automated visits away.
crete-municipal-clerk.wanted: The appointed Village Clerk's name, and the village hall's street address and phone.

cumberland-county-board.summary: Cumberland County's precincts are on the map; its three board districts aren't, so the card can't say which one you're in. All six members are named on the county's site.
cumberland-county-board.why: The county publishes no district boundary, and its own certified results show two precincts split between districts, so no arrangement of whole precincts can draw them.
cumberland-county-board.wanted: Cumberland's three board district boundaries, as map data or as a map. Nothing else here is missing — form, members and precincts are all in hand.

dewitt-township-officials.summary: De Witt County township cards name your township but not the people who run it.
dewitt-township-officials.why: The county's township officials list is a scan whose layout makes it impossible to say which name holds which office without guessing.
dewitt-township-officials.wanted: The same list in any typed form, with each officer's role clearly attached to their name.

dupage-municipal-phones.summary: DuPage municipal cards don't show a phone number.
dupage-municipal-phones.why: The regional mayors' directory prints seven-digit numbers with no area code, so showing them would mean guessing what to dial.
dupage-municipal-phones.wanted: A DuPage directory that prints full ten-digit numbers, or an official statement of each municipality's area code.

dupage-ward-cities.area: Wood Dale, Oakbrook Terrace and Warrenville
dupage-ward-cities.summary: Ward lines aren't drawn for Wood Dale, Oakbrook Terrace or Warrenville, so those cards can't tell you which ward you live in.
dupage-ward-cities.why: The only dataset covering the three was last updated in 2021 and may predate the redraw after the 2020 census, so its lines could be the old ones.
dupage-ward-cities.wanted: Ward boundaries published by each city, or each city's adopted redistricting ordinance so the older county lines can be checked against it.

edwards-county-precincts.summary: Edwards County's voting precincts aren't shown.
edwards-county-precincts.why: The County Clerk says the county's precinct boundaries exist on paper only, so there is no map file anywhere to publish.
edwards-county-precincts.wanted: The county's precincts digitised — or a paper precinct map clear enough to line up against real streets.

effingham-municipal-officials.summary: Effingham County's 12 cities and villages appear on the map without their mayors, presidents or council members.
effingham-municipal-officials.why: Nobody publishes a county-wide list of municipal officials, and the county's own directory covers its departments rather than its towns.
effingham-municipal-officials.wanted: A roster of the 12 municipalities' mayors, presidents and councils — from the county, or from the towns themselves.

fayette-county-board-geometry.summary: Fayette County's seven board districts aren't drawn, so the card can't say which one you're in. The county does name all 14 members with party and term.
fayette-county-board-geometry.why: The county's own published map divides one precinct between two districts and leaves the line between two others undrawn, so it doesn't place every part of the county.
fayette-county-board-geometry.wanted: The map file behind the county's printed district map — or written answers on where the Avena line runs and which western precincts sit in districts 2 and 6.

ford-county-board-vintage.summary: Ford County's three board districts aren't drawn, so the card can't say which one you're in. The county does list which townships make up each district.
ford-county-board-vintage.why: One precinct is shared between two districts, and the only published map is titled 2011 with nothing saying whether it is still the plan in force.
ford-county-board-vintage.wanted: Which plan is in force, and how the Patton 3 precinct divides between districts 1 and 3. The township list is otherwise ready to use.

gallatin-board-contact.summary: Gallatin County's five board members are named, and three of the five have no published phone number or e-mail address at all.
gallatin-board-contact.why: The county publishes a phone for two of the five and an e-mail for none, and nothing gets invented to fill the blanks.
gallatin-board-contact.wanted: County-published phone numbers and e-mail addresses for the five members — especially the three who currently have neither.

grundy-special-districts.summary: Grundy County's fire, park and library districts aren't shown.
grundy-special-districts.why: The county's mapping carries no boundary for any of them — its fire section is empty — though the clerk's directory does name the districts and their trustees.
grundy-special-districts.wanted: Fire, park and library district boundaries as map data. The trustees are already published and ready to go alongside.

hamilton-municipal-officials.summary: Hamilton County's towns show on the map without their mayors, presidents or council members.
hamilton-municipal-officials.why: Neither the county's website nor its mapping carries a list of municipal officials, and no other source for one has turned up.
hamilton-municipal-officials.wanted: A roster of the municipalities' presidents, mayors and councils — a county directory of officials would cover it.

hardin-county-board.summary: Hardin County's commissioners aren't named. They're elected county-wide, so there are no districts to draw — only the list of who holds the seats is missing. Its voting precincts do show.
hardin-county-board.why: The county's published web address leads to a parked page, so no county source names the sitting commissioners. Election results name who won, not who holds a seat today.
hardin-county-board.wanted: A county-published list of the sitting commissioners. That is the whole ask — there is no map to look for here.

henderson-county-website.summary: Nothing is shown for Henderson County — not its board districts, not its precincts.
henderson-county-website.why: The web address published for the county is a parked domain with no county site behind it, and no map data for the county exists anywhere public.
henderson-county-website.wanted: Whether the county has a website at all, and whether its board districts and precincts exist as map data. The clerk's e-mail does work.

jasper-county-board.summary: Jasper County's three board districts aren't drawn, so the card can't tell you which one you're in. The county does publish which townships and precincts make up each.
jasper-county-board.why: Every district line follows a township line except inside Wade township, where four precincts fan out from Newton and no published map draws their rural edges.
jasper-county-board.wanted: Wade township's four precinct boundaries in full — the rural parts, not just the city wards. Everything else about these districts is in hand.

jersey-county-board-districts.summary: Jersey County's four board districts aren't drawn, so the card can't say which one you're in. All twelve members are named with their district.
jersey-county-board-districts.why: The only district map the county publishes is dated 2016 — before the redraw every Illinois county did in 2021 — and there is no data file behind it.
jersey-county-board-districts.wanted: Whether that 2016 map is still the plan in force, and the map file behind it. A list of which precincts make up each district would also do.

jodaviess-jersey-precinct-geometry.summary: Jersey County's voting precincts aren't shown.
jodaviess-jersey-precinct-geometry.why: The county publishes no precinct boundaries, and it merged precincts after 2020, so the census map that would otherwise stand in is out of date — and two of the old precincts vanished into others without the county saying which.
jodaviess-jersey-precinct-geometry.wanted: Where Jersey 9 and Jersey 10 went — which of Jersey 1 through 8 absorbed them. Current precinct boundaries from the county would do it too.

johnson-county-board.summary: Johnson County's commissioners aren't named. They're elected county-wide, so there are no districts to draw — the list of who holds the seats is what's missing.
johnson-county-board.why: The county's website refuses every automated visit, and certified election results name who won a race rather than who holds the seat today.
johnson-county-board.wanted: A county-published list of Johnson's sitting commissioners. The precincts are already on the map, and there is no board map to look for.

joliet-municipal-contact.summary: Joliet's council contact details are refreshed by hand rather than automatically, so a change can take longer to show up here.
joliet-municipal-contact.why: The city's site opens normally in a browser but refuses automated requests, so the list has to be kept current the slow way.
joliet-municipal-contact.wanted: A council list the city is willing to publish in a form a program can read.

kankakee-city-wards.summary: Kankakee's seven city wards aren't drawn — the city's own data holds ten shapes for seven wards, and one address can land in two of them.
kankakee-city-wards.why: The data mixes the old ward map with the new one and doesn't mark which is which, and the city's approved 2022 map is a picture no program can read.
kankakee-city-wards.wanted: A clean set of current shapes for the seven wards, or confirmation from the city of which duplicates are the 2022 ones.

kankakee-municipal-officials.summary: Kankakee County's 21 towns show a name and a link, with no mayor, village president or council members.
kankakee-municipal-officials.why: No county-published directory of municipal officials exists, and the contact fields in the county's own municipal data are empty for all 21.
kankakee-municipal-officials.wanted: Any county or regional directory naming mayors, village presidents and boards — ideally one republished after each election.

kankakee-special-districts.summary: Kankakee County's fire, park and library district cards show a name and nothing else — no address, phone or website.
kankakee-special-districts.why: The county's data has contact fields for every one of these districts and leaves all of them empty.
kankakee-special-districts.wanted: A Kankakee directory of fire protection, park and library districts with contact details.

knox-precinct-geometry.summary: Knox County's voting precincts aren't drawn, though its five board districts are.
knox-precinct-geometry.why: All but one of the county's precincts can be located today; the exception is Knox Township, which went from seven precincts to six and nothing published says which became which.
knox-precinct-geometry.wanted: How Knox Township's seven precincts became six — a map, a written description, or word of which old precinct went into which new one. That single fact makes the whole county buildable.

lake-municipal-names.summary: Lake County's 41 towns show a village hall address, phone and website, but name no mayor, president or trustees.
lake-municipal-names.why: No county or regional body publishes municipal officeholder names, and the county's own site now challenges automated visits.
lake-municipal-names.wanted: A Lake County or regional directory naming each municipality's head of government and board.

lasalle-board-districts-stale.summary: LaSalle County's board districts are assembled here from precincts rather than taken from a county map, and eleven split precincts are drawn whole — so about 1,659 residents see the neighbouring district.
lasalle-board-districts-stale.why: The county publishes no map of the districts it adopted for 2022-2031, so the lines are built from the precincts its recent elections were actually run under.
lasalle-board-districts-stale.wanted: The county publishing its adopted 2022-2031 districts as map data, which would retire our version outright.

lasalle-municipal-wards.summary: La Salle, Peru and Earlville elect aldermen by ward, and none of those three ward maps can be drawn here. Mendota's are shown.
lasalle-municipal-wards.why: All three publish ward maps a person can look at but no program can read, and Peru's own code still describes wards drawn before the 2010 census.
lasalle-municipal-wards.wanted: Ward boundaries as map data from any of the three — or confirmation that Earlville's 2025 map is its current adopted plan.

lawrence-county-board.summary: Lawrence County's seven board districts aren't drawn, so the card can't say which one you're in. All seven members are named on the county's own site.
lawrence-county-board.why: The county's mapping carries taxing districts only — no board districts, no voting precincts — and no published election results describe the districts either.
lawrence-county-board.wanted: The seven districts as map data, or a description of which townships and part-townships make up each. A precinct map would do as well.

lee-municipal-officials.summary: Lee County's 13 towns show a name and a link only, with no mayor, president or trustees.
lee-municipal-officials.why: The County Clerk confirmed in writing that the county publishes no directory of municipal officials in any form.
lee-municipal-officials.wanted: Any Lee County list pairing a town with its mayor or president — a clerk's yearbook, a regional directory, or contacts added to the county's municipal data.

lee-park-library-districts.summary: Lee County's park districts aren't shown. Its fire and library districts are.
lee-park-library-districts.why: The county's mapping carries fire service areas and no park boundaries of any kind.
lee-park-library-districts.wanted: Park district boundaries from the county's mapping system.

library-districts-unmapped-counties.summary: Most Illinois counties show no library district at all — 66 of the 91 this site serves. Only six of them had a note on file saying so before today.
library-districts-unmapped-counties.why: The layer is built county by county from each county's own map data, and most counties publish none. Nothing was tracking how many that left unanswered.
library-districts-unmapped-counties.wanted: Nothing from readers — one measured statewide source already answers for all 68. What is missing is the decision on how to ship it: 68 dispatch entries, or one statewide entry carrying a 2-3 MB file.

livingston-precincts.summary: Livingston County's voting precincts aren't shown.
livingston-precincts.why: The county runs no public mapping system and publishes no precinct boundaries in any form — its yearbook lists the precincts as text only.
livingston-precincts.wanted: Precinct boundaries from any county-published source. The yearbook's polling place list is ready to attach to them.

livingston-special-districts.summary: Livingston County's fire, park and library districts aren't shown.
livingston-special-districts.why: The county publishes no free boundary data. Its parcel fabric is sold as shapefiles, and whether that fabric carries a district column is unmeasured until it is bought or the county is asked.
livingston-special-districts.wanted: County-wide fire, park and library district boundaries from any official source. The yearbook already supplies the contacts.

logan-fire-districts.summary: Logan County's fire protection districts aren't shown.
logan-fire-districts.why: The county's only fire boundaries are emergency dispatch zones cut into compass quadrants, and joining them back together doesn't match any adopted district.
logan-fire-districts.wanted: Adopted fire protection district boundaries. The county yearbook supplies the contacts the day boundaries exist.

macon-board-phone-area-code.summary: Macon County board members' phone numbers show as seven digits with no area code, because that is how the county publishes them.
macon-board-phone-area-code.why: The county lists home and cell numbers without an area code. Most of the county is 217, but a mobile can be issued anywhere and a wrong guess reaches a stranger.
macon-board-phone-area-code.wanted: The members' numbers with area codes, from the county's own page or a clerk's list. Nothing else on this roster is missing.

macon-district-name-formatting.summary: Macon County's fire, park and library districts show with the spaces missing from their names — MtZion, MarrowBone — because that is how the county publishes them.
macon-district-name-formatting.why: Putting the spaces back automatically would invent names: the same rule that fixes MtZion turns MarrowBone into “Marrow Bone”, which is nothing's name.
macon-district-name-formatting.wanted: The districts' names as the county actually spells them, or the same map layers republished with the spaces intact.

macoupin-county-board-districts.summary: Macoupin County's nine board districts aren't drawn, so the card can't say which one you're in. Its voting precincts are on the map.
macoupin-county-board-districts.why: The county publishes district maps a person can read but no data behind them, and its precinct data doesn't say which district each precinct belongs to.
macoupin-county-board-districts.wanted: District boundaries as map data, or a table pairing each precinct with its district. The member list is already in hand and waiting.

macoupin-special-districts.summary: Macoupin County's fire and park districts aren't shown. Its eleven library bodies are.
macoupin-special-districts.why: The county's data portal carries no boundary but precincts and school districts, and the clerk's map room holds election maps only — though the same portal does carry the Clerk's tax report naming which districts every tax code pays.
macoupin-special-districts.wanted: A Macoupin parcel layer, or any map, carrying the county’s tax codes — that alone would draw all fifteen fire districts and the park district from the Clerk’s own report. The libraries already ship from a statewide source.

macoupin-ward-geometry.summary: Eight Macoupin cities elect aldermen by ward. Their council members are named here; the ward lines aren't drawn.
macoupin-ward-geometry.why: None of the eight publishes ward boundaries as map data, and Carlinville's written street-by-street description predates the 2020 census.
macoupin-ward-geometry.wanted: Ward boundaries as map data for any of the eight — or, for Carlinville, whether it redrew its wards after the 2020 census.

madison-ward-officials.summary: Madison County ward cards name your alderperson in five of its six ward cities. In the City of Madison the card gives the ward and no name.
madison-ward-officials.why: The county's ward map leaves its contact fields empty, so the names come from the regional officials directory — which lists the City of Madison's eight council members without saying which ward each holds.
madison-ward-officials.wanted: Which ward each of the City of Madison's eight council members represents — from the city, or filled into the county's own OFFICIAL column, which exists on all 31 ward rows and is empty on every one.

marion-county-board-districts.summary: Marion County's five board districts aren't drawn, so the card can't say which one you're in.
marion-county-board-districts.why: The county publishes no district map, and Centralia and Salem are each split across three districts, so the census boundaries that would stand in can't be placed.
marion-county-board-districts.wanted: The county's board districts as map data — or which census precincts make up each of the current Centralia and Salem precincts.

marshall-precinct-geometry.summary: Marshall County's 14 voting precincts aren't drawn. Its board districts are.
marshall-precinct-geometry.why: The county's only precinct map is a PDF, and two precincts cut through towns rather than following township lines, so census boundaries can't rebuild them.
marshall-precinct-geometry.wanted: Marshall County's precinct boundaries as map data, plus polling places if the county publishes them.

mason-precinct-vintage.summary: Mason County's 21 precincts are drawn from 2020 census boundaries. The county's current polling list names the same 21, so the names and the count check out — whether a line has moved doesn't.
mason-precinct-vintage.why: The county publishes no precinct map of its own, and a polling list can't show whether a boundary moved without a name changing.
mason-precinct-vintage.wanted: A yes or no from the Clerk on whether any precinct boundary has moved since 2020 — and if one has, the precinct map.

massac-precinct-geometry.summary: Massac County's three commissioners are named on the County card, but its 17 voting precincts aren't drawn.
massac-precinct-geometry.why: The county publishes no map data of any kind — no precinct boundaries, no polling place map, no mapping system at all.
massac-precinct-geometry.wanted: The 17 precinct boundaries in any form, even a scanned paper map — or the Clerk's word that they exist on paper only.

mchenry-park-district.summary: McHenry County's park districts aren't shown — the one metro county where they can't be.
mchenry-park-district.why: The county's mapping publishes individual parks and facilities rather than the boundaries of the districts that run them.
mchenry-park-district.wanted: Park district boundaries on the county's mapping system.

mchenry-ward-cities.summary: Harvard and Marengo both elect by ward, and neither city's wards can be shown here.
mchenry-ward-cities.why: Harvard's website refuses automated visits, no public source carries either city's ward boundaries, and how Marengo's wards are arranged isn't confirmed anywhere official.
mchenry-ward-cities.wanted: Ward boundaries for either city from an official source, plus a plain description of how each city's wards are laid out.

mclean-special-districts.summary: McLean County's fire, park and library districts aren't shown.
mclean-special-districts.why: The county publishes detailed election mapping and no boundary for any of these districts — its park layers are individual facilities, not district lines.
mclean-special-districts.wanted: Fire, park and library district boundaries. The clerk's trustee lists are already published and ready to attach.

momence-ward-geometry.summary: Momence's four wards aren't drawn, though its eight alderpersons are named.
momence-ward-geometry.why: The city's only ward map is an image last changed in 2017, before the 2020 census, and nothing newer is published anywhere.
momence-ward-geometry.wanted: Momence's adopted ward boundaries as map data. The seats are already published.

morris-ward-geometry.summary: Morris's four wards aren't drawn, though its eight aldermen are named.
morris-ward-geometry.why: The city's wards are defined in a 2013 ordinance whose only copy is a scan, and no map data for them exists at either the city or the county.
morris-ward-geometry.wanted: Morris's ward boundaries as map data, or a readable copy of the ordinance's written ward descriptions — which the city code says are the definition that governs.

municipal-website-dead-ends.area: Morris, Calumet Park, Chatham and Rochester
municipal-website-dead-ends.summary: Four town cards — Morris, Calumet Park, Chatham and Rochester — link a website that opens to nothing: a for-sale page, a blank page, and two unconfigured servers.
municipal-website-dead-ends.why: Each county publishes that address as the town's official website, and a link that answers but shows nothing looks perfectly healthy to an automated check.
municipal-website-dead-ends.wanted: Each town's working web address, from the town itself or its county clerk, so the county directories this app reads can be corrected.

ogle-lasalle-special-districts.summary: Fire, park and library districts aren't shown in Ogle or LaSalle County, though both counties levy taxes for them.
ogle-lasalle-special-districts.why: Neither county publishes a boundary for any of them. Both publish the districts' names and tax rates, and a name is not a boundary.
ogle-lasalle-special-districts.wanted: Fire, park and library district boundaries from either county as map data — the same territory they already maintain in order to levy those taxes.

ogle-municipal-wards.summary: Byron and Polo both elect by ward, and neither city's ward lines can be drawn. Their aldermen are named.
ogle-municipal-wards.why: Byron's ward maps are pictures no program can trace, and Polo publishes nothing about its wards at all.
ogle-municipal-wards.wanted: Ward boundaries as map data from either city — or Byron's adopting ordinance, which would confirm its 2023 maps are the post-2020 redraw they look like.

park-city-wards.summary: Park City's three wards aren't drawn — the one ward-electing city in Lake County with no published boundaries.
park-city-wards.why: The city's site carries no ward map or ward list, and the wards appear in no county or public source either.
park-city-wards.wanted: Park City's ward boundaries as map data.

pass10-frontier-unasked.summary: Warren County's voting precincts aren't drawn, so there is no precinct card there. Its board districts do show.
pass10-frontier-unasked.why: The county doesn't publish its precinct boundaries as map data anywhere findable, and the election-results vendor that settled other counties doesn't carry it.
pass10-frontier-unasked.wanted: Warren County's voting precincts as map data, or a precinct list its certified results name. The County Clerk has a working e-mail address, and asking has worked before.

pass9-ward-seats-without-maps.area: Chillicothe, West Peoria, Colona, Galva, Geneseo, Beardstown and Virginia
pass9-ward-seats-without-maps.summary: Seven cities name their council members by ward while the map can't show where those wards are. Five have boundaries in hand that are 1.7-8% short of their own city limits; two have none at all.
pass9-ward-seats-without-maps.why: Every boundary found for the five predates the 2020 census and no city says whether it redrew, and Cass County publishes no map data at all for the other two.
pass9-ward-seats-without-maps.wanted: Each of the five held city clerks confirming whether its wards were redrawn after the 2020 census, and where the lines run in the ground annexed since — plus ward boundaries for Beardstown and Virginia, which have none at all.

peoria-fire-park-library-contact.summary: Peoria County's fire, park and library cards link each district's own website but name no trustee, address or phone.
peoria-fire-park-library-contact.why: The county's data carries a name and a link and no contact details, and nobody publishes a list of the trustees who run these districts.
peoria-fire-park-library-contact.wanted: A trustee list or contact details keyed to each district. The boundaries and the districts' own links are already here.

perry-county-website-blocked.summary: Perry County's precincts are on the map, but its three commissioners aren't named. They're elected county-wide, so there are no districts to draw.
perry-county-website-blocked.why: The county's website turns away automated visits, and it is the only source that says who currently holds the three seats.
perry-county-website-blocked.wanted: A county-published list of Perry's sitting commissioners — or the county's site answering automated clients, which would supply it.

pike-precinct-geometry.summary: Pike County's 31 voting precincts aren't drawn. Its nine commissioners, elected county-wide, do show on the County card.
pike-precinct-geometry.why: The county runs no mapping system of its own and publishes its precincts as names only, inside election results.
pike-precinct-geometry.wanted: Pike County's precinct boundaries as map data, plus polling places if the county publishes them.

plano-ward-officials.summary: Plano's four wards are drawn, but the card names no alderman for them.
plano-ward-officials.why: No city or county source lists Plano's aldermen by ward — the county yearbook goes only as deep as the mayor and clerk.
plano-ward-officials.wanted: A Plano aldermen-by-ward list, plus confirmation that the January 2022 ward boundaries survived redistricting.

pope-county-board.summary: Nothing is shown for Pope County's board — not districts, not commissioners.
pope-county-board.why: No county document has been read at all. The county's web address serves a template page with no county information on it, and no map data for the county exists anywhere public.
pope-county-board.wanted: Whether the board is elected by district or county-wide — then either the district boundaries as map data, or the commissioners' names from a county source.

putnam-precinct-geometry.summary: Putnam County's voting precincts aren't drawn. Its five commissioners, elected county-wide, do show on the County card.
putnam-precinct-geometry.why: Illinois's smallest county runs no mapping system, and publishes its precincts and polling places as documents rather than as data.
putnam-precinct-geometry.wanted: Putnam County's precinct boundaries as map data, or a polling place list keyed by precinct.

quincy-ward-officeholders.summary: Quincy's seven wards are drawn, but the card names no alderman for them.
quincy-ward-officeholders.why: The city's website turns away automated visits, and the one city archive that is readable names aldermen without ever saying which ward each of them holds.
quincy-ward-officeholders.wanted: Quincy's council roster BY WARD, from any source a program is allowed to read. Names alone aren't enough — this card answers which ward you're in.

randolph-fire-park-library.summary: Randolph County's fire and park districts aren't shown. Its nine libraries are.
randolph-fire-park-library.why: The county's only county-wide fire shapes are 911 dispatch zones, and showing one of those as a fire protection district would misstate who levies your tax. No park boundaries exist on its account at all.
randolph-fire-park-library.wanted: Fire protection and park boundaries as the taxing districts they actually are.

randolph-precinct-polling.summary: Randolph County precinct cards name your precinct and nothing else — not even where you vote.
randolph-precinct-polling.why: The county's precinct data has a polling place field and leaves it blank on all 35 rows, and no separate polling place list is published.
randolph-precinct-polling.wanted: Polling places filled in on the precinct data, or any clerk's list pairing precincts with polling places.

rock-island-andalusia-township-library.summary: Andalusia Township shows no library, though the township elects a library board and a statewide layer now draws one.
rock-island-andalusia-township-library.why: The county's own library map draws nine of its ten library bodies and omits this one. The boundary that exists comes from a broadband contractor, and Rock Island's card is built from the county's own map instead.
rock-island-andalusia-township-library.wanted: The Andalusia Township Library's service boundary from the county or the township — or a decision to mix publishers inside one county's card, which nothing here does today.

rockford-city-precincts.summary: Voting precincts show everywhere in Winnebago County except inside Rockford.
rockford-city-precincts.why: Rockford runs its own election board, so the county's precinct map stops at the city line, and the city's precincts are published as lists rather than boundaries.
rockford-city-precincts.wanted: Precinct boundaries from the Rockford Board of Election Commissioners, or a city precinct layer on the county's mapping system.

saline-precinct-geometry.summary: Saline County's 13 board members are named on the County card — they're elected county-wide — but its 28 voting precincts aren't drawn.
saline-precinct-geometry.why: The county publishes a polling place list and no precinct boundary of any kind.
saline-precinct-geometry.wanted: The 28 precinct boundaries in any form, even a scanned paper map — or the Clerk's word that they exist on paper only.

sangamon-park-library-districts.summary: Sangamon County's park districts aren't shown, though their trustees are published in full. Its libraries are shown.
sangamon-park-library-districts.why: None of the county's published map data carries a park district boundary.
sangamon-park-library-districts.wanted: Park district boundaries — from the county or from the districts. The trustee lists are already in hand.

scott-county-commissioners.summary: Scott County's three commissioners aren't named. They're elected county-wide, so there are no districts to draw.
scott-county-commissioners.why: The county's own page renders its member list through a widget that returns nothing, and election results name who won a race rather than who holds the seat today.
scott-county-commissioners.wanted: Confirmation of which three commissioners are serving now, and which of them chairs the board. No map needed.

st-clair-board-contact.summary: St. Clair County board cards name your member and nothing else — no direct phone number or e-mail.
st-clair-board-contact.why: The county's board pages give one shared mailbox and switchboard for all 28 districts and publish no contact details for individual members.
st-clair-board-contact.wanted: Any county-published phone number or e-mail for individual board members.

st-clair-park-library-districts.summary: St. Clair County's park districts aren't shown. Its nineteen libraries are.
st-clair-park-library-districts.why: The county's mapping carries no park district boundary anywhere in it.
st-clair-park-library-districts.wanted: Published park district boundaries for St. Clair County.

stephenson-freeport-precincts.summary: Stephenson County's four Freeport Township board districts are traced from the county's printed map rather than built from data, so they're accurate to about 20 metres. The card says so.
stephenson-freeport-precincts.why: The Clerk confirmed her office holds no digital precinct file — the printed maps are the county's own copy — and the regional consortium that holds the data sells it rather than publishing it.
stephenson-freeport-precincts.wanted: Freeport Township's 16 precincts as map data, from whoever holds a digital copy of them.

stephenson-park-library-districts.summary: Stephenson County's park districts aren't shown, though its fire and library districts are.
stephenson-park-library-districts.why: The county's only maps of them are 2014 pictures in which the districts are shading rather than lines, so nothing accurate can be traced from them.
stephenson-park-library-districts.wanted: Park district boundaries as map data — each of the four districts holds its own, and none has been asked.

vermilion-precinct-geometry.summary: Vermilion County's voting precincts aren't drawn, though its nine board districts now are.
vermilion-precinct-geometry.why: The only precinct map the county publishes as data was drawn before it consolidated its precincts, so it shows eighty-four where the county now runs sixty.
vermilion-precinct-geometry.wanted: A current precinct map as data from Vermilion County GIS, asked 24 Aug 2026, or from either election authority — the Clerk for the 38 outside Danville, the Election Commission for the 22 inside it.

wabash-precinct-geometry.summary: Wabash County's three commissioners are named on the County card — they're elected county-wide — but its voting precincts aren't drawn.
wabash-precinct-geometry.why: The county has no website to publish anything on, and the Clerk hasn't yet said whether precinct boundaries exist as a file or only on paper.
wabash-precinct-geometry.wanted: The precinct boundaries in any form, even a scanned paper map — or the Clerk's word that they exist on paper only.

washington-precinct-geometry.summary: Washington County's voting precincts aren't drawn. Its board districts are.
washington-precinct-geometry.why: The county runs no mapping system, and publishes its precinct and polling place maps as pictures only.
washington-precinct-geometry.wanted: Washington County's precinct boundaries as map data, plus polling places if the county publishes them.

wenona-two-clerks-disagree.summary: Wenona sits in two counties whose clerks publish different city councils. The card shows Marshall County's list, so three people LaSalle names aren't shown and four officials show no phone number.
wenona-two-clerks-disagree.why: Only Marshall's clerk has said where her list comes from — the city itself — while LaSalle's directory states no source at all.
wenona-two-clerks-disagree.wanted: LaSalle's clerk saying where her Wenona list comes from, or the city publishing its own council.

white-special-districts.summary: White County's fire, park and library districts aren't shown. Its board districts, precincts, members and polling places all are.
white-special-districts.why: The county runs no mapping beyond a parcel search, and nothing it publishes names a boundary for any of these districts.
white-special-districts.wanted: Any adopted boundary for the county's fire, park or library districts — from the Clerk, the 911 office, or a district's own filing.

whiteside-municipal-officials.summary: Whiteside County's 11 towns name a mayor and a clerk with contact details, and none of them names a council or village board.
whiteside-municipal-officials.why: The county yearbook those names come from covers mayors and clerks, and lists no aldermen or village trustees anywhere in it.
whiteside-municipal-officials.wanted: The eleven municipalities' councils and village boards, from the cities' own pages or from another county document.

whiteside-precinct-polling.summary: All 60 Whiteside precincts name a polling place and address — two of those locations came from the County Clerk by e-mail, because the county's published list still omits them.
whiteside-precinct-polling.why: Four precincts point at buildings the county's polling place list doesn't carry. The Clerk named them, and the card says where that came from.
whiteside-precinct-polling.wanted: The two missing voting locations added to the county's own published list, which would retire the two records carried here by hand.

whiteside-special-district-boards.summary: Nobody publishes who runs Whiteside County's 25 fire, park and library districts.
whiteside-special-district-boards.why: The county names all 25 bodies in its Clerk's tax report, and no county document names a trustee, an address or a telephone number for any of them.
whiteside-special-district-boards.wanted: Trustees, an address or a phone for any of Whiteside’s 25 fire, park and library districts — from the district itself or from a county list. The boundaries are built but held back under the county's licence.

whiteside-special-districts.summary: Whiteside County's fire, park and library districts aren't shown. The county sells its map data and its licence forbids publishing anything built from it.
whiteside-special-districts.why: Everything needed to draw these districts is public, and the county's own licence agreement forbids redistributing a product derived from it — so the boundaries exist here and are not published, pending the county's written permission.
whiteside-special-districts.wanted: Written permission to display boundaries derived from the county's parcel data — or a fire, park and library district layer the county publishes without the licence. The derivation is already done and gated.

winnebago-special-districts.summary: Winnebago County's fire, park and library districts aren't shown.
winnebago-special-districts.why: The county’s fire district map is published only as a picture, and the only county-wide fire data is 911 dispatch zones — showing a dispatch zone as a fire protection district would misstate who levies your tax.
winnebago-special-districts.wanted: Fire, park or library district boundaries as data from WinGIS or another Winnebago agency, with written permission to display them — the consortium’s licence otherwise forbids redistributing anything derived from its data.

woodford-special-district-boards.summary: Woodford County's 26 fire, park and library district cards name the district and nothing else — no trustee, address, phone or website.
woodford-special-district-boards.why: The boundaries come from the county's parcel map, which carries the district's name and no contact of any kind, and the county publishes no list of the people who run these districts.
woodford-special-district-boards.wanted: Trustees, an address or a phone for any of Woodford's 26 fire, park and library districts — from the district itself or from a county list. The boundaries are already here.
